reason: The event this book was built for landed exactly as underwritten, three trading days ago, so there is nothing to reassess and everything to lose by touching it. The 2026-09-16 FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on a 12-0 vote, and 16 of 18 dots see at least one more hike this year, with futures pricing ~4.2% fed funds by December and ~4.6% by September 2027. That is the single best backdrop a floating-rate carry book can have: JAAA and FLOT coupons reset upward off 3M SOFR over the coming quarter at zero duration cost, while the 10Y at 5.00% and 30Y at 5.36% are punishing anyone taking the duration side of that trade. All four legs entered 2026-09-16 and all four are green (JAAA +0.06, AMLP +0.46, FLOT +0.08, SPYI +1.16); none is within a mile of its stop. The credit backdrop is benign rather than stressed: IG spreads ~81bp, Q2 US CLO issuance $126.5B across 285 deals on tightening AAA spreads, and US defaults projected to fall to 3.0% by October from 5.3% a year earlier. The AMLP sleeve is the working leg, not the problem leg: ~7.3% distribution yield, +23% YTD, with EIA putting Brent near $90 in 2H26 and midstream cash flows fee-based rather than price-levered. The one real case for trading was cash drag, and I priced it and rejected it. JAAA's 30-day SEC yield is 4.63% (09/18) against the engine's 4.00% fixed cash, so redeploying the 16% cash buys roughly 10bp a year on NAV, about 0.2bp a week. A complete replacement book is the only instrument I have, and the brief is explicit that it costs real basis points -- at 2bp per side across 84% gross that is several bp of certain, immediate loss to chase a fraction of a bp of weekly gain. Break-even is measured in months, not weeks. That arithmetic is also the diagnosis of this book's -1.66% NAV: eight legs in nine weeks, in a strategy whose entire edge is uninterrupted accrual. A carry book does not lose to the market on security selection, it loses to its own turnover, and I am not paying that toll again three days into a position that is doing what it was designed to do. The 16% cash is not idle either -- with the long end repricing and spreads at multi-decade tights, it is the buffer that lets me add into a credit air pocket rather than be forced to sell AAA paper into one. Hold, let the coupons reset, and keep the powder.
